messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — saw a meaningful perf regression on contbatch after the kernel-selector roll. throughput down ~12% on our longctx workload, p50 latency up.
jin: Which env? any repros/sha?
maria: staging-dedicated. repro is longctx-200k tokens with continuous batching enabled. I grabbed profiler snapshots and a heap diff.
oliver: Can you paste the top of the flame? my money's on KV page churn + merge stalls (HOL) :eyes:
maria: top lines from the flame:
```\ntop:\rruntime::kv_merge_wait 41%\nbatcher::merge_coalesce 22%\nkernel_selector::choose 6%\n``` 
sanjay: sounds like merges are spending a lot of time waiting on kv reclamation. we've seen similar when eviction becomes serialised on a shard lock. :thinking:
jin: I ran a quick trace — lots of contbatch merges hitting head-of-line in the kv_pager while eviction is active. snippet from logs:
```\n[2026-03-18T10:12:01Z] [kv_pager] evict_start shard=7\n[2026-03-18T10:12:01Z] [contbatch] merge_wait shard=7 wait_ms=12\n[2026-03-18T10:12:01Z] [contbatch] merge_wait shard=7 wait_ms=18\n[2026-03-18T10:12:02Z] [kv_pager] reclaim_done shard=7\n``` 
oliver: Right — recall we changed eviction to async-reclaim which ends up serialising on the shard mutex. Also kernel-selector now prefers a bigger GEMM kernel for perf which temporarily increases scratch working set -> more eviction pressure.
maria: @sanjay any quick heuristics we can try? ideally without reverting kernel changes.
sanjay: Proposal: add a lightweight 'merge-throttle' heuristic. If kv_shard.reclaim_inflight > 0 then avoid merging batches that would target that shard — either split the merge or push smaller forward merges. Pseudo:
```\nif reclaim_inflight(shard) > 0:\n  split_merge(batch_group)\nelse:\n  coalesce(batch_group)\n``` 
jin: Also suggest an orthogonal kernel tweak: for long contexts prefer `kernel=low-scratch` path to reduce working set. Quick AB: default vs low-scratch on the same load.
oliver: +1 on both. We should also add a metric kv.merge_wait_ms and a rollout gate that refuses kernel-selector default if kv.merge_wait_ms.p50 > 8ms. And spin a canary with contbatch_merge_enabled=false for a subset of clients.
maria: I'll wire up the merge_throttle + kernel flag on a staging canary and run the longctx suite. Uploading flame snapshots and heap histos to #artifacts. Thanks :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/staging/kv-throttle-3445009876 by maria
jin: Quick first canary results look promising — throughput recovered ~9%, mem growth flattened on the 30m run. Need multiple runs to be confident.
maria: Good. I'll keep capturing kv_shard.flags and batch_id in traces so we can correlate evictions -> merge_wait. Will follow up with perf graphs tomorrow.
